title: Paint a Street With No Matching Neighbours
statement:
A street has n houses in a row. Each one must be painted red, green or blue. costs[i] is a list of three prices: painting house i red, green and blue, in that order.

Two houses next to each other may not have the same colour. Return the minimum total cost to paint every house.

examples.why: Green, red, blue costs 2 + 7 + 3. Taking the cheapest allowed colour house by house gives green, blue, red = 2 + 6 + 5 = 13, so greedy loses.
A single house has no neighbours; any colour works.
Both houses want red, but only one can have it.

hints: Deciding a house's colour only matters to the next house. What is the smallest thing you need to remember about the houses so far?
For each colour c, keep the cheapest way to paint houses 0..i with house i painted c.
best[i][c] = costs[i][c] + the smaller of best[i − 1] for the two other colours. Only the previous row is needed.

explain.intuition:
Greedy fails because a cheap choice now can block a much cheaper choice next door. But the only thing house i + 1 cares about is the colour of house i. So for every colour, remember the cheapest way to paint the street up to house i ending in that colour. Three numbers summarise the whole past.

To extend to the next house in colour c, you add its price for c to the best of the other two colours from the previous step. Rolling three variables forward gives O(1) memory.
steps: Set r, g, b to the prices of house 0.
For every next house with prices [cr, cg, cb]: new r = cr + min(g, b), new g = cg + min(r, b), new b = cb + min(r, g). Compute all three from the old values.
pitfalls: Updating r in place and then using the new r to compute g. Take all three from the previous house.
Picking the cheapest allowed colour house by house, as in the first example.
Returning only the last house's red value instead of the minimum over all three colours.

solutions.title: Try every colouring
solutions.idea: Recursively choose a colour for each house that differs from the previous one and keep the cheapest total.

solutions.title: Three running totals
solutions.idea: Keep the cheapest cost so far ending in each colour, and build the next house's three values from the previous ones.

followups: There are k colours instead of 3. How do you keep each step O(k) instead of O(k²)? (Hint: remember the smallest and second smallest.)
The houses stand in a circle, so the first and last are neighbours too.
